false_success_traps: A recheck once reported the listing as removed while it was still on the page. Look at the page itself before calling it gone.
A security check page, a captcha notice, or any "required field" or "invalid" message after you submit means the request did not go through.
General privacy wording on the page is not a confirmation. The page must say the request itself was received or submitted.
If the form is still showing after you submit and no receipt appears, nothing was sent.
The "check your email" page is not the end. The request stays open until the emailed link is followed.
genuine_confirmation: After the last step the page plainly says the removal request was received or submitted, and asks you to check your email for a confirmation link. The request is not finished until that link is opened.
name: Veripages

opt_out_url_check.note: A plain request got a "Just a moment..." browser check (HTTP 403). A real browser is needed.

steps: Have the link to your own listing page ready. It must be the page for one person. A link to a page of search results is rejected.
Open the Veripages privacy control page in a normal browser. Solve the human check if one appears.
Press Next until the page asks for the link to the profile.
Paste the link to your listing and press Next. If the page says the link is not valid, stop and get the right link.
Press Next or Skip until the page asks for your name and email.
On the opt-out form, fill in the name on the listing and an email address you can read.
Solve the human check, then send the form.
Wait for the page to say the request was received and to check your email.
Open the email from Veripages and follow the confirmation link.
Check the listing again later to see that it is gone.
